summary:
Both selected fixes are done and the AI shopping Tester now passes 5/5 (was 4/5).

**1. Machine-readable product data (Find products, Compare options)**
- Product pages now embed a `<script type="application/ld+json">` Product object (name, description, image, sku, url, and an Offer with price, priceCurrency INR, availability InStock/OutOfStock and url). It's built in the `/product/<slug>` route from the live SQLite catalogue — the sku and price come from the product's first pack variant, so nothing is hard-coded.
- New `/sitemap.xml` lists the homepage, all category pages and all 25 product URLs, read from the database at request time.
- New `/llms.txt` (Markdown) with the store name, a one-line summary, a `## Products` list of `- [Name](absolute product URL): ₹price` lines (from the same `product_rows()` helper the listings use), and a `## How to buy` section explaining the add-to-cart form (with its csrf_token), the shareable checkout link and the no-account checkout.
- All URLs are absolute, built from the request via a small `absolute_url()` helper (`url_for(..., _external=True)`) — no domain is hard-coded, so it works locally and in production.

**2. Shareable checkout link (Checkout link)**
- The cart page's Checkout link now carries the cart in the URL: `/checkout?items=SKU:QTY,SKU:QTY` (SKUs, never prices). Below the ₹299 minimum the previously dead "Checkout" button is now a working "Review checkout" link with the same parameter.
- On `GET /checkout?items=…` the route rebuilds that visitor's session cart from the parameter: each id is looked up as a SKU first, then as a product slug (taking the smallest pack); unknown ids and out-of-stock products are ignored and quantities are clamped to the site's existing 1–20 range. Normal checkout without the parameter is unchanged.
- The ₹299 minimum order rule is kept: a below-minimum cart now renders the checkout page with the full order summary (product names, quantities, totals) plus the notice, instead of bouncing the agent back to the cart; only placing the order stays blocked. Checkout is already guest-only (no accounts), so no sign-in step was needed.

No dependencies added, no design/price/product changes, and CSRF on all forms is untouched — agents use the page's own token like a browser would.
